ledger.note: 947: Boson II, Count of Arles, establishes the County of Provence as a fief of the Kingdom of Arles. Infobox: '947 (Boson II, Count of Arles, established)'; the borders ran 'south from the Rhône to Nice and north from Embrun to the Vivarais'. The six departments of the region Provence are my drawing of that description.

1112: Douce, heiress of Provence, marries Ramon Berenguer III of Barcelona and the county passes to the Catalan house. 'in between married Douce, heiress of Provence (1112)'; he was 'count of Provence in the Holy Roman Empire, from 1112'; the County page says the house ruled 'until 1246'.

ledger.note: 1125: the county is partitioned and the lands north of the Durance go to the Count of Toulouse as a marquisate. 'This led to a long-standing Toulouse claim to the county, finally resolved by partition in 1125'; the county 'was divided into a marquisate north of the Durance' (Alphonse-Jourdain of Toulouse and Raymond-Berenger). The page lists no towns; Vaucluse, the upper Durance (Forcalquier) and the Hautes-Alpes are my reading of 'north of the Durance'.

1193: the partition between the County of Provence and the County of Forcalquier ends with Alfonso II's marriage. County page: 'In 1193, Alfonso II of Provence married Gersande of Sabran, granddaughter of William II, Count of Forcalquier' and the partition 'was ended by an intra-dynastic marriage in 1193'; Beatrice later 'inherited the two counties of Provence and Forcalquier'. Alpes-de-Haute-Provence is my reading of Forcalquier. [Reviewer eu-10-x, 2026-10-25] moved from 1246, which the page gives only for the Angevin succession.

1246: Charles of Anjou becomes count and the Angevins rule until 1382 (Beatrice is listed as countess 1245-1267, Charles I 1246-1285). List of rulers: 'Charles I: 1246 to 1285'; County page: 'It was the latter who inherited the two counties of Provence and Forcalquier'.

notes:
Written for eu-10-x from five pages (County of Provence, Marquisate of Provence, County of Nice, Ramon Berenguer III, List of rulers of Provence; the page 'List_of_counts_of_Provence' does not exist). None gives an area. The infobox start 947 is the County page's; the earlier Boson kingdom (879) and the Kingdom of Arles are the Cliopatria rows Lower Burgundy / Kingdom of Lower Burgundy / Kingdom of Arles (other groups).
STRUCTURE: Cliopatria lacks Provence as a state. This dossier draws the county as six departments of the region Provence; the 1125 partition removes Vaucluse, Alpes-de-Haute-Provence and Hautes-Alpes (north of the Durance, the marquisate of Toulouse, later the Comtat Venaissin by 1274), the 1193 union with Forcalquier (moved from 1246 by reviewer eu-10-x: the County page dates the end of the Forcalquier partition to the 1193 marriage) returns Alpes-de-Haute-Provence, the 1388 dedication removes the Nice disc. Hautes-Alpes (Embrun) and Vaucluse never return in the pages read.
END YEAR: the county ends in December 1481 so that the royal-domain-of-france dossier (Crown lands page, 1481) and this one do not both hold Provence; the County page's own dates are 1486 (incorporation) and 1487 (annexation).
DISAGREEMENTS: the List of rulers says Ramon Berenguer I the Great in its table and Ramon Berenguer III in its text for the 1112 marriage; the Marquisate page gives no founding date; the Arles line (975 marquis) and the 947 count's succession (Bosonids, Rotbalds) are given without a clean list, so rulers start at 1112.
NOT DRAWN: the 1229 Treaty of Paris cession of the Toulouse lands west of the Rhone (not county land); the 1271-1274 passage of the marquisate to Philip III and Gregory X (Comtat Venaissin, its own Cliopatria row); Orange as a principality from 1181 (Principality of Orange, Cliopatria 1260-1571); the Baux wars and the 1166 Aragonese succession (not on the pages read).
Counterparts without dossiers: County of Forcalquier; the Nice/Ubaye lands are in the County of Savoy dossier (eu-13). Gazetteer: 'Nice' as a place may be missing.
